pr_title: Refactor LIFX discovery to prevent duplicate discovery response handling
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Avi Miller <me@dje.li>

## Proposed change

Refactor LIFX discovery again to ensure that devices that disconnect are properly reconnected on rediscovery while maintaining in-flight checks to prevent duplicate discovery handling.

pr_comments: @bdraco any chance of a review and merge, please?

This looks to be the fix to the issues I have remaining. Great work and thank you a ton.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59674699/170803162-e37c1fe1-e003-4dc9-940e-be7b57453377.png)

Thanks for fixing this problem! It cost me multiple hours until I found out that the new HA version was the root cause. 
Note: This is _not_ non-standard behavior from a lifx point of view. This happens every time you turn a lifx bulp off/on via a physical wall switch that disconnects the bulp (which is a common use case for lifx bulps)
Can this be merged?

> Can this be merged?

No. The current proposed solution trades one problem for another which will fix the issue for one set of network conditions, but likely result in breakage for other network conditions.  The race condition needs to be solved so we don't end up doing another followup to address any side effects that this change could bring as-is.  We want to avoid a situation where one release works for some users, then we make a change and it breaks a different set of users, and then we make another change and it breaks for original users, etc....
I'm still working on this, but something is blocking rediscovery when we lock inflight discoveries and I'm having a hard time narrowing down what, why and when.

Ok, I've refactored the refactor so that we reconnect to existing devices that have disconnected after initial discovery while also maintaining in-flight checks to ensure that we only process each discovery once per device.
Now available in the LIFX Beta component for testing purposes: https://github.com/Djelibeybi/ha-lifx-beta/releases/tag/2022.06.04

Something for the future.  

The TPLink, which is also one of the older integrations in HA, had all of these problems in the past until we switched the **to the config entry per connection model** and let HA take care of all the retry and discovery logic via the config flows in #56701.  I should note that the change didn't make a lot of people happy (any change does that) until they realized how it when from very unreliable to rock solid after a few months.

That's usually the long term solution I recommend to avoid rebuilding all the logic HA already has internally in each integration as its so much fun to try to handle every race condition that core has already had to come up with solutions for.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/56701/files#diff-d4422fb3884b7038f40208c93fd0627a775a9946c166d9b75d260e47683dea88

> The TPLink, which is also one of the older integrations in HA, had all of these problems in the past until we switched the **to the config entry per connection model** 

I didn't think this was an option, but I'm glad to hear it is. My Photons integration uses this method and it's way easier to handle each bulb as its own config entry. I'm going to keep working on that as an eventual replacement for the `aiolifx`-based core integration as I'm way more familiar with Photons and its capabilities (which are numerous).

I think where you had the check was fine. Instead I think the only change was to check again right after the lock is acquired to prevent the duplicate updates issues when the 2nd/3rd etc discovery that were waiting for the 1st one acquired the lock but the entity has already been created and is in a good state since

> Instead I think the only change was to check again right after the lock is acquired

If the idea is to allow a subsequent discovery to succeed if the first one fails, then I'm not sure checking right after the lock is the right place. Wouldn't we want to check after it sucessfully connecting to the bulb? To be honest, I didn't get any non-unique ID errors where it was and where it is, so it's hard to be sure that it's working properly without letting it run for a few hours.

> > Instead I think the only change was to check again right after the lock is acquired
> 
> 
> 
> If the idea is to allow a subsequent discovery to succeed if the first one fails, then I'm not sure checking right after the lock is the right place. Wouldn't we want to check after it sucessfully connecting to the bulb? 

That's pretty much when the check will happen on the 2nd/3rd/ etc discovery since it happens right after the 1st one releases the lock allowing the waiting 2rd/3rd etc to proceed after 1st successfully connected and got the entity in a good state.


> To be honest, I didn't get any non-unique ID errors where it was and where it is, so it's hard to be sure that it's working properly without letting it run for a few hours.
Ok, I have to do other stuff for a while, but I'll try and get back to this later today/tomorrow.

I managed to create a test instance that generated duplicate discoveries and finally refactored to the point where those discoveries did not trigger any non-unique or missing entity ID errors. This relies on the source of `unique_id` not being dependent on a successful bulb discovery.

issue_context.title: Lifx lights going unavailable until restart since Lifx discovery refactor in 2022.5
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Crux of the issue is, since upgrading to 2022.5 the Lifx integration is now partially broken and putting entries into the log, this never used to occur.
Lights now never become available after being turned off and back on until HA is restarted and the lights are currently on. Seems once they get turned off, HA is no longer able to see them even when they come back on.

I can confirm the lights work from the Lifx app, and they are cloud connected and respond. Other lights that remain with the power on, continue to function.
Only HA reporting the lights unavailable.

Log entries:

1. Updating lifx light took longer than the scheduled update interval 0:00:10

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12243212/172025235-8986a663-786e-4818-8abf-587bd55127ac.png)

2. Duplicate LIFX discovery response ignored

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12243212/172025409-6cb9e4bf-ba38-4f26-b634-2427cf4cea9f.png)

Evidence of lights as showing unavailable, even though these lights are currently on.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12243212/172025267-5dc334fa-4391-47f3-85a4-4136abfc3a84.png)

Happy to provide any additional information required to help resolve this one.

Possibly the same as #72120 and #72827 

Lifx discovery was of no issue before the refactor, so it is directly related to that update.

Perhaps revert until this is properly tested.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.5.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.4.6

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Lifx

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/lifx

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

Issue 2:

Integration: LIFX (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 4 June 2022, 06:30:48 (2 occurrences)
Last logged: 4 June 2022, 06:30:48

Duplicate LIFX discovery response ignored
```

I never delete the entity, so I don't need to recreate it. It always exists, I just change it's availability status.

```suggestion

                # Multiple discoveries in-flight at the same
                # time and this one lost the race and the first
                # one already created the entity
                _LOGGER.debug("Already created %s", entity.who)

```

```suggestion
                return

```
That might be better though if you don't want to try again to create the entity, but I think you might want to based on the issue reports

Since one of the reported problems is concurrent discoveries, Here's the exact problem I'm concerned about here:

Discovery 1 happens for bulb A, it wins and gets the lock via `async with inflight.lock:`
Discovery 2 happens for bulb A again, it loses the race and waits for `async with inflight.lock:`
Discovery 3 happens for bulb A again, it loses the race and waits for `async with inflight.lock:`
Discovery 4 happens for bulb A again, it loses the race and waits for `async with inflight.lock:`
Discovery 1 proceeds and creates the entity
Discovery 2 proceeds and the entity is already created so it hits https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/72213/files#diff-71a06a9aebb8a8734257fa1b6545e754d5c23ee87d5c05ec92133498c8afea3cR463
Discovery 3 proceeds and the entity is already created so it hits https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/72213/files#diff-71a06a9aebb8a8734257fa1b6545e754d5c23ee87d5c05ec92133498c8afea3cR463
Discovery 4 proceeds and the entity is already created so it hits https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/72213/files#diff-71a06a9aebb8a8734257fa1b6545e754d5c23ee87d5c05ec92133498c8afea3cR463

We could end up polling the bulb 4 (or more) times in quick succession which could overwhelm the device.

It's not so much that concurrent discoveries are a problem, it was an issue with dropping the entity when discovery failed. The next round attempted to recreate the entity, which threw a "doesn't generate unique entity IDs" error. 

This refactor eliminates that error by not dropping the entity from `LIFXManager`'s `self.entities` array. It just marks the entity unavailable. If the user manually deletes the entity, the device is deleted and discovery works just fine if the bulb reappears.
So I think add the guard in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/72213#discussion_r894233205 and to return only if entity is already available, and this PR should be good go.
